findings: All 31 production-window captures were reviewed individually: 21 main journey images, five draft recovery images and five work-control images. The journeys use the current debug executable in disposable signed Mac app bundles and the same source hashes. Light and dark views keep messages, controls and keyboard focus readable; at 800 × 680 the Send button wraps to its own visible row.

The five work captures show an admitted run, requested pause while its current item finishes, a paused boundary in both appearances, retained completion and current-reply cancellation. Boundary controls reflect the actual run and disable while their request is pending. A second resident cannot start competing work; returning to the owner retains its state. A new conversation keeps completed work visible.

The work journey passes 25 checks: start, pause at the boundary, one more item followed by pause, resume, finish the current item and stop, a bounded Next run, cancellation of only the current reply and native Quit. The owner excludes competing admission before mutation, retains the agent selected by the session, and joins provider, gate and checkpoint work before releasing admission.

The saved-history dialog retains its scrolling content and reserved Close action. Native pointer Close, reopen, exact retained text and subsequent Resume pass. Focus can scroll the heading partly out of view; selected context and Close remain usable. Saved-message Save and Discard actions remain visible.

The draft captures show exact multilingual text, restored source-file selections and clipboard image preview, saved status and focus in both appearances. The narrow attachment list scrolls without hiding Add files, Discard or Send. Failed saving keeps the message editable after refused Quit and presents Retry guidance. Successful Retry clears save and Quit notices.

The draft receipt passes 59 checks across four launches, covering two working copies and two providers. A final edit followed immediately by Quit reopens intact; 32 rapid native Unicode edits recover the final revision after interruption. Discard remains durable, appearance and reduced motion restore, normal Quit retains each conversation's spending record, and recovery sends no unintended prompt.

Attachment captures show image previews, names, sizes, removal and a text preview disclosure. Native picker selection and cancellation, clipboard images, file-URL drag, exact text/image delivery, and changed/missing/unsupported file refusal pass. Rich views retain headings, emphasis, quotes, lists, code, multilingual text and visible link focus. Unsupported pipe-table syntax stays plain selectable text; narrow horizontal code scrolling was not exercised.

Native selection and the scrolled reading anchor remain stable while replies and an earlier tool update. Latest clears selection and resumes following. Copying preserves complete reply, tool and conversation source bytes. Native keyboard link activation reaches the controlled localhost destination and closes only that test tab. Authored HTML and unsafe links remain literal, and remote images make no request.

Known issues remain assigned to native accessibility work: Latest reply overlaps text or Copy message in some captures, Choose model touches the Agent focus ring, and unavailable-provider/refused-resume guidance includes nested technical error chains. Narrow side-panel content requires vertical scrolling. These checks do not claim those issues are resolved.

The main receipt passes 172 checks and records keyboard-to-accessible-reply latency. Japanese Kana ミニくらみ was composed and committed as an unsent draft in this run. VoiceOver was not running. This does not establish spoken-reader usability, reliable IME activation, candidate panels, Romanization, Chinese or Korean input, high-contrast behavior, Linux parity or a whole-application performance budget.

Conversation commands are addressed by resident session and logical conversation; work controls additionally require the admitted run identity. Source-bound journeys cover drafts, saved history, resident switches and work boundaries. Focused Rust and JavaScript tests cover stale controls, repeated requests, gate boundaries, transcript pruning/reseed, refusal and orderly shutdown.

The native Appearance observer now waits for an enabled popup, an observable menu item and its committed value. Light and Dark selections pass in all three journeys; fixed sleeps and two independent accessibility presses are no longer used for that selection.
